question: What is California's statewide minimum wage per hour in 2026?
answer:
California's statewide minimum wage is $16.90 per hour in 2026, effective January 1, 2026, for all employers regardless of size [4][5][6]. The California Department of Industrial Relations' FAQ, as quoted in one source, says the rate applies to all employers "not otherwise covered by a higher minimum wage specific to an industry or a locality" [6].

One source gives $16.50 for 2026, but it states that rate took effect January 1, 2025, and its figures are labeled 2025 [3]. The other sources, including the most recent ones from September and October 2026, agree on $16.90, so $16.90 is the better-supported figure [4][5][6]. The rate is set under California Labor Code section 1182.12 [4][6]. It is scheduled to rise to $17.40 on January 1, 2027, as certified by the Department of Finance on July 31, 2026 [5][6].

Higher rates apply to some localities and industries, such as fast food workers at $20.00 per hour [4][5]. Many cities and counties also set their own higher rates [4][5]. This covers California only, and rules differ in other jurisdictions. This is general legal information, not legal advice. A specific situation needs a licensed lawyer.

studyNotes.focus: The question asks for California's statewide minimum wage rate in effect during 2026.

keyPoints.text: California's statewide minimum wage is $16.90 per hour in 2026 for all employers, effective January 1, 2026.
The 2026 rate is set under Labor Code 1182.12, which indexes the wage annually to CPI-W.
The rate rises to $17.40 per hour on January 1, 2027, as certified by the Director of Finance on July 31, 2026.
California has no tip credit, so tipped workers must receive the full minimum wage before tips.

conflicts.text: Source 4 states the 2026 statewide minimum wage is $16.90/hr, while source 3 states it is $16.50/hr (its figure is the 2025 rate, effective January 1, 2025).

mayBeStale.text: Source 3 gives $16.50 per hour as the statewide rate, which was the 2025 rate and is superseded by the 2026 rate of $16.90.
Source 2 (Congress.gov CRS report, 2016) reports the federal and state figures from its own date and is outdated for current rates.
